elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence: "may be exercised with respect to a Party no more than once per year" — a once-per-year cap on audits of a Party is equivalent to once in any 12-month period.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted language provides only "not less than fifteen (15) days' prior notice", and does not require the notice to be written.
No business-hours limitation appears in 9.8, 9.9 or the inserted sentence.

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: Audit rights are exercised by "Any Party" through the F&ASC (a committee of the Parties); no independent auditor is required.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Neither the retained text nor the insertion imposes confidentiality obligations on the reviewing Party or the F&ASC.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No location or off-site preference is stated; audits are simply of "books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs" via F&ASC procedures.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 9.8: the audited Party "shall be permitted to recover, from the Party or Parties requesting the review or audit, the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying" — the requesting (Vendor-side) Party bears costs with no underpayment exception, which is at least as favourable as the element.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: The right is limited to reviewing "books, records, vouchers, and accounts of costs" exercised through the F&ASC's procedures; no system or remote access is granted, so no deletion of access language was needed.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence expressly caps exercise "with respect to a Party no more than once per year"; deterministic check "audit frequency limited" passes.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Inserted sentence requires "not less than fifteen (15) days' prior notice to the Party whose books, records, vouchers, and accounts are to be reviewed or audited"; the fallback does not require written form.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained 9.8 shifts "the entire costs reasonably incurred in complying" onto the requesting Party unconditionally, so the requesting counterparty bears audit cost with no underpayment carve-out at all.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: the single inserted sentence supplies the once-per-year frequency cap and the fifteen (15) days' prior notice floor, and retained Subparagraph 9.8 already places the entire compliance cost on the requesting Party with no underpayment exception, which is at least as favourable as "Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent".

Preferred level remains incomplete (notice is 15 not 30 days and not stated to be written; no business-hours, independent-auditor, auditor-confidentiality or off-site-where-possible requirements), so the finding is correctly pitched at deviation with a fallback redline rather than claiming the preferred position.

Minimality holds: nothing was deleted, the favourable reciprocal cost-recovery mechanic and the F&ASC channelling in 9.9 were retained, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, confidentiality or access boilerplate) were added beyond the two selected fallback parameters.

Intent preserved: the insertion sets floors that operate alongside 9.9's requirement that audits be exercised through the F&ASC in accordance with its procedures, and leaves Schedule B proportional cost allocation for Management Committee audits intact, with no undefined terms or dangling cross-references.
Drafting nit only (not a defect requiring repair): the new sentence is unnumbered — consider designating it as Subparagraph 9.10 for citation cleanliness.
